sentences.text:
This is the seventh application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.327/2019, registered at Police Station-Kotwali District Anuppur (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 317, 354, 354(d), 376, 376(2)(n), 506, 201,
120-B, 313, 419, 34 of IPC and section 3, 5(2) of the Medical Termination of Preganancy Act and under section 3, 5(1), 4 and 6 of POCSO Act.
2. Learned counsel appearing for applicant submitted that applicant and prosecutrix were having love affairs and later on prosecutrix delivered a baby and had lodged FIR against the applicant.
Applicant is in custody since 3 1/2 years.
Trial is likely to take some more time.
Considering the period of custody, applicant may be released on bail.

sentences.text: 3. Learned Government Advocate appearing for the State opposed the application for grant of bail and submitted that prosecutrix has been examined in the court and she has supported the prosecution case.
Considering the same, application be dismissed.
4. Heard the counsel for the parties.
5 . Applicant is in jail since last 3 1/2 years.
Trial will take some more time to conclude.
Considering the period of custody of applicant, bail application filed by applicant is allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/-(Rs. Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court for his appearance before the trial court on the dates to be fixed by the trial court.

7. The applicant shall also abide by the conditions of Section 437 (3) of Cr. P. C. C.C. as per rules (VISHAL DHAGAT) JUDGE tarun Umesh Kumar @ Umesh Yadav vs State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146937069/
